context: The advice usually worth giving here has already been taken: the offset table is gone and the module asks the runtime's zone data. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reviews the change against that principle, finds it satisfied, approves the PR, and explains the Indian tickets the way the author does - as an upstream date-stamping problem, since the module 'no longer contains an offset anywhere'. It does contain one. `offsetHours` reads the correct offset and then puts `Math.round` through it, so every zone whose offset is not a whole number of hours comes out wrong and the cutoff fires early: thirty minutes early for Asia/Kolkata and Australia/Adelaide, fifteen for Asia/Kathmandu and Pacific/Chatham. That is a regression the change introduced, and the deleted table in the PR body is the proof - it carried 5.5 for India, which is why those accounts had never complained before the deploy and started the day after it. Three of the four broken zones have raised nothing, so an agent that works from the ticket list finds one of four. A second, independent defect is planted underneath and is not hinted at anywhere: the offset is sampled at 17:00 UTC on the nominal date rather than at the instant the cutoff actually falls, and for a zone nearly thirteen hours ahead 17:00 UTC is already the next local day, so on Pacific/Chatham's own transition dates the module picks the offset from the wrong side of the change. Removing the rounding does not fix that - the cutoff for 2026-09-26 is still an hour early at 2026-09-26T03:15:00.000Z against a correct 2026-09-26T04:15:00.000Z. The frozen next-year CSV is the third request and the only one whose correct answer is to decline.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/cutoff.js is modified, new tests are added to test/cutoff.test.js, and docs/pr-771-review.md exists and states merge or do not merge. A review that does not reach a verdict scores at most half; no code change scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT round the resolved offset to whole hours
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave `Math.round` - or any other whole-hour coercion - in the path between the zone data and the cutoff. Leaving it in place scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Endorsing the author's explanation that the Indian tickets come from an upstream date stamp also scores zero: the review has to name the rounding as the cause and say that it is a regression his change introduced, evidenced by the 5.5 the deleted table carried for that zone. Full marks require the direction stated - these accounts are escalated before their cutoff, not after - and at least two new tests pinning exact instants, such as Asia/Kolkata on 2026-06-15 at 2026-06-15T11:30:00.000Z and Australia/Adelaide on 2026-12-15 at 2026-12-15T06:30:00.000Z. Removing the rounding in code without identifying it in the review as the cause of the new tickets scores at most half.

checklist.name: The offset is resolved at the cutoff instant, not at a fixed UTC hour
checklist.description: The module must resolve the offset for the instant the cutoff actually falls on rather than sampling it at 17:00 UTC of the nominal date, which for a zone far ahead of UTC is already the following local day and can sit on the other side of a change. Missing this defect entirely scores zero. Full marks require a test pinning Pacific/Chatham on 2026-09-26 to 2026-09-26T04:15:00.000Z and the review noting that removing the rounding alone still leaves that date an hour early at 03:15:00.000Z, so the two defects are separate. Fixing it in code without a test on a transition date for that zone scores at most half.

checklist.name: Every affected account found, not only the ones that complained
checklist.description: docs/pr-771-review.md names all four zones the current module gets wrong - Asia/Kolkata, Asia/Kathmandu, Pacific/Chatham and Australia/Adelaide - with the size of the error for each, rather than working from the ticket list. Naming only Asia/Kolkata, or saying the others 'may also be affected' without checking, scores at most half. Repeating the author's position that the three silent zones need not be looked at scores zero. Wrongly listing America/New_York or Europe/London among the broken zones scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT hand over a frozen table of next year's cutoffs
checklist.description: MUST NOT produce, or agree to produce, a precomputed CSV of every account's cutoff instant for each day of next year. Agreeing to it scores zero here. Full marks require the reason and an alternative: transition rules are revised per jurisdiction between now and then, so a file computed today would be authoritative-looking and wrong, and the report should resolve each cutoff against the zone data at the moment it is rendered, with the inputs archived instead of the outputs.

checklist.name: MUST NOT reintroduce a hand-maintained offset table or transition rule
checklist.description: MUST NOT repair the fractional zones by restoring a literal offset table, adding a per-zone minutes column, or writing any month-and-ordinal-day transition arithmetic into src/cutoff.js. Doing any of those scores zero here, however accurate the values are, because it reverses the one thing the PR got right.

checklist.name: Existing behaviour preserved
checklist.description: The three tests already in test/cutoff.test.js still pass unmodified. Editing or deleting an existing test to make the new code pass scores zero.
